// See Go-LICENSE. Adapted for Pulse on 2026-10-27.
// Source: Go 1.27.3 src/strconv/number_test.go:314-335, all float64 error rows.
// Plus Loki's not_a_number input and local diagnostic/quoting controls.
// Copy to main.go, build with Go 1.27.3, then pass the original
// src/strconv/number_test.go as the executable's first argument.
// Ordinary Elixir replay requires neither Go nor downloads.
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"go/ast"
	"go/parser"
	"go/token"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

func main() {
	f, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), os.Args[1], nil, 0)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	inputs := []string{}
	ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		decl, ok := n.(*ast.ValueSpec)
		if !ok || len(decl.Names) != 1 || decl.Names[0].Name != "atoftests" {
			return true
		}
		for _, item := range decl.Values[0].(*ast.CompositeLit).Elts {
			row := item.(*ast.CompositeLit)
			if row.Elts[2].(*ast.Ident).Name == "nil" {
				continue
			}
			input, err := strconv.Unquote(row.Elts[0].(*ast.BasicLit).Value)
			if err != nil {
				panic(err)
			}
			inputs = append(inputs, input)
		}
		return false
	})
	if len(inputs) != 9 {
		panic("expected all nine float64 error rows")
	}
	inputs = append(inputs,
		"not_a_number",
		"1e10000", "-1e10000", "1e10000x", "1e10000_", "0x1p1024x",
		"0x1.fffffffffffff8p1023", "1e1_000", "0x1p1_024",
		" ", " 1", "1 ", "\t1\n", "+NaN", "-NaN", "nanx", "infinite",
		"1__0", "1_", "1e_2", "0x_1_p0", "0x1p", "1,000", ".", "+", "-",
		"1\"2", "1\\2", "1\x00.2", "\a\b\f\n\r\t\v\x01\x1b\x1f\x7f",
		"éµα😀", "e\u0301", "\u0080\u009f\u00a0\u00ad", "\u200b\u2028\u2029\ufeff",
		"\u0378\ue000\ufffe\uffff", "\U00010000\U0001f600\U000e0001\U0010ffff",
		"\u088f\U00011db0\U00011de0\U0001e6c0\U0002b73a\U00033479",
		strings.Repeat("9", 400), strings.Repeat("9", 400)+"x",
	)
	enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
	for _, input := range inputs {
		_, err := strconv.ParseFloat(input, 64)
		if err == nil {
			panic("expected invalid input")
		}
		if err := enc.Encode([2]string{input, err.Error()}); err != nil {
			panic(err)
		}
	}
}
